title: Release audit: The redactor recognizes the French password label only as the whitespace-separat
summary: Treat the joined forms as the French password label: fold case and diacritics and accept whitespace, `-` and `_` between the words in `_secret_label`/`_phrase_end` (or normalize the label before matching). Add direct and session-level tests asserting that a value following `mot_de_passe`, `mot-de-passe` or `MOT_DE_PASSE` is absent from both the displayed and the retained text.
requirements: The French password label is recognized as a secret label when written as separate words, when joined with underscores, and when joined with hyphens, regardless of letter case.
A value adjacent to a joined French password label is redacted with the same placeholder used for other secret values and is not present in the rendered message nor in the retained session text.

Redaction of a joined French password label works with the value forms and separators already handled for the spaced form: delimited assignment, colon or equals separator, quoted values, bare values, and a label wrapped in quotes or brackets.
A joined French password label with no adjacent value does not cause any part of the surrounding message to be redacted.
All previously supported secret labels in every supported language continue to be redacted exactly as before.
acceptance: For a message containing a hyphen-joined French password label followed by a value, the rendered output and the retained session text contain the redaction placeholder instead of the value.
For a message containing an underscore-joined French password label followed by a value, the rendered output and the retained session text contain the redaction placeholder instead of the value.
The spaced French password label and all other supported secret labels still redact as before.
A joined French password label without an adjacent value leaves the message unchanged.
Quoted and bracketed joined French password labels are redacted the same way as their spaced equivalents.
plan_goal: Forgel Code: interactive agent client instead of a command wrapper

result.summary: Closed the release-audit leak: the French password label is now recognised as a secret label in its joined spellings. In `forgel_code/interactive.py` a helper `_joined_phrase` treats a compound label whose segments are `mot`/`mots`, `de`, `passe` joined only by `_` or `-` (case-insensitively, diacritics folded, as for every other label) as the same several-word secret label as the spaced form, and `_secret_label` consults it. Because recognition feeds the existing `_binding`/`_descriptor_span` path, every value form already handled for the spaced label is redacted with the unchanged `[redacted]` placeholder: colon/equals separators and their runs, delimited and bracketed assignments, quoted values, bare values, copulas, and quoted or bracketed labels — on both the display and the retention paths, which share `redact`. A joined label with no adjacent value binds nothing, so the message stays unchanged. Added `tests/test_redact_french_joined.py` covering underscore- and hyphen-joined labels (plus mixed case), each value form, equivalence with the spaced form, prose without a value, unchanged behaviour of the other labels, idempotence, and session-level rendering and retention of replies, state and errors. Recorded the fix under Unreleased/Fixed in `CHANGELOG.md`. Tested with `python -m pytest -q` (final run: 378 passed, 600 subtests passed) and with a focused run of the new module (9 passed, 72 subtests passed).
assumptions: The joined spellings to support are exactly underscore-joined and hyphen-joined, as the specification states; a dot-joined `mot.de.passe` is deliberately not treated as the label.
Only the joined French password label is added: the secret-word and stem vocabularies, the placeholder, the context rules and the spaced phrase handling are untouched.
Mixed joiners inside one label are accepted (for example `mot_de-passe`), since the requirement distinguishes only which separators may appear.
The CHANGELOG entry is documentation and is verified by review; no test reads it.
